help.intro: Nine prepositions — an, auf, hinter, in, neben, über, unter, vor, zwischen — can take either the dative or the accusative, and the sentence decides which. When they answer wo? (where is it? — a position, nothing moving), they take the dative: Das Buch liegt auf dem Tisch. Die Katze sitzt unter dem Bett. Das Bild hängt an der Wand. The verbs that go with this side are the verbs of being somewhere: stehen, liegen, sitzen, hängen, sein, bleiben, wohnen. This is the rule that separates a learner who knows the dative from one who can use it; the accusative half (wohin?) is the next quiz, and the two are always learnt as a pair.
help.tips[0].text: No movement, just a place: auf dem Tisch, unter dem Bett, an der Wand, in der Küche, vor den Häusern. Contractions: an dem → am, in dem → im.
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: The book is (lying) on the table.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: We're sitting in the garden, next to the house.
help.tips[0].trap: English 'on the table' is the same whether the book lies there or you put it there. German asks first: is anything moving?
help.tips[0].check.q: Die Milch steht in ____ Kühlschrank. (der Kühlschrank)
help.tips[0].check.why: Nothing moves: the milk is just standing there, so wo? → dative, and der Kühlschrank becomes dem Kühlschrank.
help.tips[0].visual.caption: A dot: it stays where it is. Wo? asks for the dative.
help.tips[1].title: The verbs of position
help.tips[1].text: stehen (stand), liegen (lie), sitzen (sit), hängen (hang), sein, bleiben, wohnen, arbeiten — if the verb describes being somewhere, the preposition after it takes the dative.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: The lamp stands on the desk. The poster hangs above the bed.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: The children are sitting at the table, and the dog is lying under the chair.
help.tips[1].check.why: wohnen is a verb of being somewhere, so the preposition takes the dative: die Stadt → in der Stadt.
help.tips[2].title: The cat on the box
help.tips[2].text: Die Katze sitzt auf der Box — sitting, dative. (In the next quiz she jumps auf die Box — moving, accusative.) Picture her sitting still whenever you see wo?.
help.tips[2].examples[0].en: Where is the cat? – On the box.
help.tips[2].examples[1].en: The cat is lying under the table.
help.tips[2].check.q: Wo ist der Hund? – Er liegt auf ____ Sofa. (das Sofa)
help.tips[2].check.why: Like the cat on the box, the dog is lying still — wo? → dative, and das Sofa becomes dem Sofa.
help.tips[3].title: The nine, with their meanings
help.tips[3].text: an (at, on a vertical surface), auf (on top), hinter (behind), in (in), neben (next to), über (above), unter (under), vor (in front of), zwischen (between).
help.tips[3].examples[0].en: The chair stands between the table and the window.
help.tips[3].examples[1].en: The cinema is behind the station, next to the post office.
help.tips[3].check.why: hinter means behind; vor is in front of, neben is next to, über is above.
help.remember[0]: Wo? — nothing moves — dative: auf dem, in der, an dem (am).
help.remember[1]: an – auf – hinter – in – neben – über – unter – vor – zwischen: the nine that switch.
help.context.en: My room: the bed stands against the wall, and above the bed hangs a picture. The desk stands in front of the window, the lamp stands on the desk. My books lie on the shelf, and under the bed the cat sleeps. Between the wardrobe and the door stands a chair.
help.mistakes[0].why: liegen is a position: wo? → dative dem.
help.hook: Say where everything is — the book on the table, the cat under the bed — with nine prepositions that switch case.
help.table.caption: The nine two-way prepositions
sentences[0].english: The book is on the table.
sentences[0].why: liegen is position (wo?), so the two-way preposition takes the dative: der → dem Tisch.
sentences[1].english: The cat is under the bed.
sentences[1].why: Position, no movement: dative — das → dem Bett.
sentences[2].english: The picture hangs on the wall.
sentences[2].why: hängen (it hangs there) is position: dative — die → der Wand.
sentences[3].why: wohnen is staying put: dative — in der Stadt.
sentences[4].english: The car is in front of the house.
sentences[4].why: stehen is position: dative — vor dem Haus.
sentences[5].english: The lamp hangs over the table.
sentences[5].why: Hanging there (wo?): dative — über dem Tisch.
sentences[6].english: The shoes are next to the door.
sentences[6].why: Standing there: dative — neben der Tür.
sentences[7].english: The garden is behind the house.
sentences[7].why: Lying there: dative — hinter dem Haus.
sentences[8].english: The table stands between the beds.
sentences[8].why: Position + plural: dative den — zwischen den Betten, with the plural's own -n.
sentences[9].english: We wait in front of the station.
sentences[9].why: Waiting is staying put: dative — vor dem Bahnhof.
sentences[10].english: The children play in the garden.
sentences[10].why: Playing IN a place (wo?): dative — in dem = im … here spelled out: dem Garten.
sentences[11].english: The dog sleeps under the chair.
sentences[11].why: Sleeping is position: dative — unter dem Stuhl.
sentences[12].english: The restaurant is next to the cinema.
sentences[13].english: The clock hangs above the door.
sentences[13].why: Hanging there: dative — über der Tür.
sentences[14].english: The bike is behind the garage.
sentences[14].why: Standing there: dative — hinter der Garage.
sentences[15].english: My key is between the cushions.
sentences[15].why: Lying between them (wo?): dative plural den — zwischen den Kissen.
sentences[16].english: The guests are already sitting in the kitchen.
sentences[16].why: Sitting is position: dative — in der Küche.
sentences[17].english: The photos hang on the walls.
sentences[17].why: Hanging there, plural: an den Wänden — dative plural den plus -n on the noun.
sentences[18].english: We wait at the traffic lights.
sentences[18].why: Waiting AT the lights (wo?): dative — an der Ampel.
sentences[19].english: A picture of Berlin hangs above the sofa.
sentences[19].why: The picture hangs there: dative — über dem Sofa.
help.tips[0].title: Wo? → Dativ: dem / der / dem / den
